summary: A. S. Ramanatha Ayyar worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He served as Epigraphical Assistant at the Archaeological Survey of India (1918–1941), Superintendent in Travancore State (1922), and held a post in the Kingdom of Thiruvithamkoor (~1924–1934).

A. V. Williams Jackson specialized in Iranian and Central Asian studies, Indology, and linguistics. He studied at Columbia University under Edward Delavan Perry and Edward Washburn Hopkins, and at Halle-Wittenberg. He served as professor at Columbia from 1895 to 1935.

Aaron P. Proffitt works in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He studied at CU Boulder, the Inter-University Center, and the University of Michigan under Micah L. Auerback, Donald S. Lopez Jr., and others. In ~2015, he joined the University at Albany, SUNY.

Abaji Vishnu Kathavate worked in the field of Indology. Succeeding Ramakrishna Gopal Bhandarkar, he held the post of Professor of Sanskrit at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute (attested 2026).

Abanindranath Tagore was an Indologist and historian-archaeologist. He studied at Sanskrit Collegiate School, Sanskrit College and University, and the Government College of Art & Craft, and later held a post at the University of Calcutta (~1921–1923).

Abdur Rehman worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied under Ahmad Hasan Dani and completed his PhD at the Australian National University under Arthur Llewellyn Basham. He was an assistant professor of archaeology at the University of Peshawar (attested 1988).

Abel Bergaigne worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied under Michel Bréal and Eugène-Louis Hauvette-Besnault (~1865–1868). He served as répétiteur at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1869–1888) and as professor at the Sorbonne and University of Paris.
Abhimanyu Rao is active in Indology. He studied under Deepak Dabral and held a post at Shiv Nadar School.

Abhiraj Rajendra Mishra is an Indologist who studied under traditional teacher Rāmbhadrācārya. He served as head of Sanskrit at Himachal Pradesh University, visiting professor at the University of Indonesia, and Vice-Chancellor of Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (~2004–2007).

Abigail I. MacBain specializes in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. She earned an MA at McMaster University, studying under Mark Rowe, James A. Benn, and Shayne Clarke, and held a post at the University of Edinburgh (attested 2026).

Abraham Hyacinthe Anquetil-Duperron worked in Indology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and religious studies. He studied at the Sorbonne, Amersfoort, and under Dastur Darab. He held posts at the Bibliothèque nationale, Académie des Inscriptions et Belles-Lettres, and Institut de France.

Abraham Sachs worked in history, archaeology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Johns Hopkins University (~1933–1937) and held positions at the Institute for Advanced Study (1945) and Brown University (~1948–1983).
Abraham Yohannan worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies as well as religious studies. He was educated at Columbia University and later held a post there from ~1894 to 1925.
Abraham Zablocki is a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies. He earned his PhD at Cornell University and held a post at Agnes Scott College (attested 2008).
Acharya Buddharakkhita studied under Mahasi Sayadaw and U Nārada, and later taught Laurence Khantipalo Mills.

Achim Bayer specializes in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He completed his MA and PhD at the University of Hamburg under David P. Jackson and Lambert Schmithausen. He worked at the University of Munich (2004–2006) and the University of Hamburg (attested 2026).

Achyutananda Dash works in Indology, philosophy, and linguistics. He was a Commonwealth Visiting Fellow at the University of Oxford (1997–1998) and held a post at Dr. Hari Singh Gour University (attested 1999).

Adalbert Bezzenberger was a linguist and Indologist. He studied under Theodor Benfey at the University of Göttingen and at Munich. After lecturing at Göttingen, he served as professor, Prorektor (1890–1891), and Rektor (1919–1921) at the University of Königsberg.

Adalbert Kuhn worked in linguistics and Indology. He studied at Humboldt University of Berlin under Franz Bopp. He had a long career at Köllnisches Gymnasium, serving as teacher, professor, and director, and joined the Prussian and Russian Academies of Sciences.

Adam Bowles specializes in Indology and religious studies. He completed his PhD at La Trobe University under Greg Bailey by 2004 and later served as a senior lecturer in Asian Religions at the University of Queensland (attested 2016–2018).
